turns.reasoning: I'm realizing the bug stems from the initial position estimate overshooting when wide characters appear early in the string, throwing off the forward-search loop. The fix would recalculate the position estimate and iteratively adjust by comparing the cell length of the truncated text against the target cut.

turns.reply:
I rewrote the search loop in `Segment._split_cells` (`rich/segment.py`) so it splits correctly when the text contains wide characters. The patch is submitted.

I haven't opened the linked Textual issue, so I don't know its exact failing input. The old code made one estimate of where the cut falls and then only searched forward from it. With wide characters near the start, that estimate could land past the cut. The new code measures the cell width at the current position and steps forward or back until it hits the cut. If the cut falls in the middle of a double-width character, that character is replaced with a space on each side, as before.

I checked it with an inline script: a Japanese string plus ASCII, split at every cut from 0 to 24. In each case the left part's cell width equals the cut (or the full width if the cut is past the end), and the two parts add up to the original width. `tests/test_segment.py` passes (49 tests). I didn't add a new test to the repo.
